function: p. 5: DDPG agent jointly sets RIS phase shifts and amplitudes, offloading ratios and resource-block allocation to minimize offloading delay; reward is uplink sum rate (Eq. 21).
system: p. 3-4, 8-9: single RIS (N=8-32 passive reflecting elements with amplitude and phase control), single-antenna AP, 4-12 vehicles, OFDMA uplink, B=1 MHz; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 5-7: DDPG actor-critic (DDPG-DM) with lightweight tabu search action refinement; reinforcement learning by interaction with the simulated MEC environment; reward is the uplink sum rate.
data_channel: p. 3, 8: custom simulator; GV-AP link Rayleigh with path loss, GV-RIS and RIS-AP links Rician (factors 2.8, 2.4); GVs move randomly in a 30x5 area; no dataset.
test_conditions: p. 7-9: trained and evaluated in one simulated environment; sweeps over 4-12 vehicles (Fig. 5), N=20-32 elements (Fig. 7), transmit power, learning rate; no separate test set.
baselines: p. 7-8: HA-A2C [38], PPO [39], DDPG [40] (all learned) and NRDDPG-DM (DDPG-DM without RIS); no non-learned or classical method in the experiments.
metrics: p. 8-10: delay (s), sum rate (bps/Hz), average reward versus training episodes (Figs. 5-12).
complexity: p. 9: proposed O(T x L D^2 + N_LTS); p. 8: baselines O(N T D), O(M K L), O(P Q R), O(S U V); no runtime.
q1_support: p. 3: "the channel gain for the direct link from GV to AP can be modeled as Rayleigh fading while considering path loss" and the reflected links "follows a Rice distribution [24]". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 9: "When k = 4, N = 28, the trend of the average cumulative reward of the five algorithms as the number of training sets increases" shows training curves in one fixed scenario; other figures sweep K, N, power and learning rate; no statement that a trained agent is tested in an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 8: "NRDDPG-DM: In the MEC environment without RIS assistance" is the proposed scheme without RIS; HA-A2C, PPO and DDPG are learned. No random or fixed RIS, SDR or optimization baseline is run; the abstract (p. 1) only claims "classical methods".
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the DDPG-DM algorithm scheme is O(T × LD2 + NLT S )"; orders of the baselines are on p. 8; no runtime or FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 7: "The position of the GV moves randomly in the range of 30 × 5" and Table I (p. 8) set a synthetic simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere (the only URL is the IEEE rights notice, p. 1).
notes: Included under area 3: the DDPG action includes the RIS phase and amplitude matrix jointly with offloading ratios and resource blocks (p. 5, A = {Theta, a_k, x_k,m}); offloading is above the physical layer, but the RIS phase is learned jointly, so above_phy does not apply. The abstract claims comparison with classical methods (p. 1) but Section IV (pp. 7-8) runs only learned benchmarks, so q3 is 0.
